statement: Whenever reverse_between head left right returns a result r, let xs be the sequence of values of head in order (xs[0],...,xs[n-1]) and let ys be the sequence of values of r in order. Then len(ys) = n, and for every integer position p with 1 <= p <= n: if p < left or p > right then ys[p-1] = xs[p-1], and if left <= p <= right then ys[p-1] = xs[left + right - p - 1].
preconditions: Let n = len(head) be the number of nodes in head. The list head is nonempty (1 <= n <= 500), every node value lies in [-500, 500], and the mathematical values of left and right satisfy 1 <= left <= right <= n.

statement: On every input satisfying the preconditions, reverse_between head left right returns a result r; it does not fail, panic, overflow, or access an out-of-range position.
preconditions: Let n = len(head) be the number of nodes in head. The list head is nonempty (1 <= n <= 500), every node value lies in [-500, 500], and the mathematical values of left and right satisfy 1 <= left <= right <= n.

statement: Whenever reverse_between head left right returns a result r, let xs be the sequence of values of head and ys the sequence of values of r. For every integer value v, the number of indices i with 0 <= i < n and xs[i] = v equals the number of indices j with 0 <= j < len(ys) and ys[j] = v.
preconditions: Let n = len(head) be the number of nodes in head. The list head is nonempty (1 <= n <= 500), every node value lies in [-500, 500], and the mathematical values of left and right satisfy 1 <= left <= right <= n.
